page_title: OpenQuack — Local-first voice dictation for macOS

summary.name: OpenQuack
summary.one_liner: A free, MIT-licensed, local-first macOS menu-bar app that transcribes speech with on-device Whisper (via WhisperKit) and pastes the text at your cursor.
keywords: transcribe speech to text on mac
use_cases: Dictating text into any app at the cursor
Speaking prompts into coding assistant or terminal prompt bars
Private offline transcription of speech on a Mac
Multilingual dictation without choosing a language
Replacing a paid dictation subscription with a free tool
summary.what_it_does: Runs as a menu-bar app on macOS: press a hotkey, speak, and the transcript is inserted where the cursor is. Transcription uses Whisper models run locally on Apple Silicon through WhisperKit and CoreML, with no account or subscription. The page reports about 2.6% word-error rate on clean speech and about 6.3% in office noise for the default model on an M4 / 16 GB Mac. It supports 99 Whisper languages with auto-detect, and mixed-language dictation. An optional setting lets you send transcription to your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which the overlay indicates when active.
notable: Fully local by default: no cloud, telemetry, or account; audio is discarded after transcription
Uses Whisper via WhisperKit/CoreML with 99 languages and auto-detect
Installable via Homebrew cask or DMG; about 8 MB app plus a speech model downloaded on first run
Published benchmark matrix covering five Whisper sizes and two engines
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later on Apple Silicon; Intel Macs are not supported
No Windows or Linux version; relies on Apple-platform technologies
First launch downloads a speech model (about 250 to 500 MB depending on RAM)
Optional cloud path: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be used instead of local transcription
